summary: Mitt Romney signed Massachusetts healthcare reform into law as governor, establishing near-universal coverage with an individual mandate.
Governor Mitt Romney and the Massachusetts legislature require all citizens to purchase health insurance.
A Rasmussen Reports poll shows Mitt Romney in fourth place among potential presidential candidates and that 43% of US voters would never consider voting for a Mormon presidential candidate.
Mitt Romney, the former Republican governor of Massachusetts, set up an exploratory committee, the first step of a presidential campaign.
Mitt Romney announced his intention to seek the Republican nomination for the 2008 presidential race.
Mitt Romney launches his campaign for the 2008 US presidency.
Article discusses Mitt Romney's political rise in Massachusetts, including his 1994 Senate challenge to Ted Kennedy and 2002 election as governor.
Mitt Romney announces he will deliver an address on faith and American society to address suspicion among Republican voters about his Mormon beliefs.
Mitt Romney gave a speech addressing Republican Party base elements about his religious beliefs during his presidential campaign.
Mitt Romney is in second place with 30% in a Zogby poll, trailing John McCain at 32%, ahead of the New Hampshire primary.
Mitt Romney and John McCain are leading the field of six Republican candidates in the final days before Tuesday's New Hampshire primary, with McCain ahead of Romney by five points in recent polls.
Mitt Romney held his final rally in Bedford, New Hampshire, before the state’s primary, warning that his race with John McCain was “razor thin.”
Mitt Romney may have lost his only real shot at the Republican presidential nomination as polls close in New Hampshire, where John McCain leads him.
Mitt Romney wins the Michigan Republican presidential primary, defeating John McCain 39% to 30%.
Mitt Romney arrived in Nevada to campaign ahead of the weekend's caucuses, leaving his Republican rivals to compete in South Carolina.
Mitt Romney is projected to win the Nevada Republican primary, following his victory in Michigan earlier in the week.
Mitt Romney finishes ahead of Rudy Giuliani in the Florida Republican primary, contributing to Giuliani's decision to abandon his White House bid.
New campaign finance reports show Mitt Romney spent $18 million of his own money in the fourth quarter of 2007, more than twice the $9.1 million he raised from outside donors.
Mitt Romney faces John McCain in the Super Tuesday Republican primary contests, with McCain leading in every state except Massachusetts.
Mitt Romney's poor showing in the Super Tuesday contests effectively ended his hopes of winning the Republican presidential nomination.
Mitt Romney's presidential campaign suffers a major defeat, winning only his home state of Massachusetts, prompting commentary on his political demise.
Mitt Romney withdrew from the Republican presidential race, effectively ceding the contest to frontrunner John McCain.
Mitt Romney endorses John McCain and urges his 288 delegates to back McCain for the Republican nomination.
Mitt Romney endorses former rival John McCain for the Republican presidential nomination and releases his 288 delegates to support McCain.
John McCain meets with Mitt Romney and two other potential running mates at his Arizona home to discuss the vice-presidential selection.
Mitt Romney was described as having been on John McCain’s original shortlist of possible running mates, but he was not selected.

Former Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney announced he will campaign in Georgia for Republican Senator Saxby Chambliss ahead of the December 2 runoff election and donated $5,000 from his Free and Strong America PAC to Chambliss's effort.
Mitt Romney won 24% of the vote in the Southern Republican leadership conference straw poll, defeating Sarah Palin who came third with 18%.
Mitt Romney comfortably won a poll of Republican delegates in New Hampshire regarding who should be the party's 2012 presidential nominee.
Mitt Romney officially confirms he will seek the Republican nomination to challenge Barack Obama in the 2012 White House race.
Mitt Romney's campaign disclosed he raised $14.2 million in the third quarter while spending an estimated $18 million over the past six months in his bid for the Republican presidential nomination.
Mitt Romney participates in a crucial GOP debate in Iowa, seeking to arrest Newt Gingrich's surge in popularity ahead of the Iowa caucuses.
Mitt Romney wins the Iowa Republican caucuses by eight votes.
Mitt Romney secured the endorsement of Senator John McCain after narrowly winning the Iowa caucuses and arrived in New Hampshire ahead of the primary.
Mitt Romney says “I like being able to fire people” while discussing health care insurers during his presidential campaign.
Mitt Romney wins the New Hampshire primary.
Republican rivals Newt Gingrich and Rick Perry attack Mitt Romney over his record at Bain Capital as he campaigns for the Republican presidential nomination.
Mitt Romney was stripped of his victory in the Iowa caucuses after a final recount showed Rick Santorum with the most votes, though the party declared the result unresolved.
Mitt Romney wins the Florida Republican primary, defeating Newt Gingrich and re-establishing himself as the party's frontrunner.
Federal Election Commission figures reveal that the Super Pac backing Mitt Romney, Restore Our Future, raised about $18 million from 200 donors during the second half of 2011.
Mitt Romney, after winning the Florida Republican primary, warned that the November White House election will be one of the most vitriolic and spiteful in US history and headed to Nevada for a rally.
Mitt Romney is expected to win the Nevada Republican caucuses, based on his 2008 performance and strong Mormon support.

Mitt Romney attempted to revive his presidential campaign by delivering a speech at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) in Washington, describing himself as "severely conservative" to win over skeptical conservatives.
Mitt Romney wins the Maine Republican caucuses with 39% of the vote, narrowly defeating Ron Paul, and wins the CPAC straw poll.
Mitt Romney delivered a much-hyped economic speech at Ford Field in Detroit that was overshadowed by a near-empty stadium and a gaffe about his wife owning two Cadillacs.
Mitt Romney wins presidential primaries in Arizona and Michigan.
Mitt Romney is expected to emerge as the clear frontrunner for the Republican presidential nomination after Super Tuesday, following his weekend win in the Washington state caucuses.
Mitt Romney is projected to win Virginia, Massachusetts, Vermont, and Idaho in the Super Tuesday primaries, with Ohio seen as decisive for his nomination prospects.
Mitt Romney won the Illinois Republican primary, defeating Rick Santorum 47% to 35%, strengthening his path to the Republican nomination.
Mitt Romney secures former Florida governor Jeb Bush's endorsement, which he describes as a key moment in the Republican presidential race.

Mitt Romney is described as the likely Republican presidential candidate for 2012, though the nomination is not officially settled and uncertainty remains over whether he will secure enough delegates before the convention.
Florida senator Marco Rubio endorses Mitt Romney for the Republican presidential nomination.
Former President George H.W. Bush is expected to endorse Mitt Romney at a campaign event in Houston, Texas.
Mitt Romney wins the Republican primary in Wisconsin over Rick Santorum.
Mitt Romney is effectively set to become the Republican presidential nominee after Rick Santorum's failure to win recent primaries, though he faces challenges uniting the party.
Rick Santorum suspends his Republican presidential campaign, leaving Mitt Romney as the clear frontrunner for the Republican nomination to face Barack Obama.

Mitt Romney enjoyed his first full day as undisputed Republican presidential candidate as several Republicans, including Marco Rubio and Bob McDonnell, ruled themselves out as his vice-presidential running mate.
The sixth anniversary of Mitt Romney signing the Massachusetts healthcare bill into law passes without major attention, as both the Romney and Obama campaigns avoid highlighting it.
Mitt Romney addresses the annual NRA conference in St. Louis, seeking the gun lobby's financial backing for his White House campaign.

Barack Obama's campaign raised $53 million in March, falling short of its $1 billion target, as Democrats anticipate an advertising onslaught from conservative Super PACs supporting the almost-certain Republican candidate Mitt Romney.
Mitt Romney selects longtime adviser Beth Myers to lead his search for a vice-presidential running mate in the 2012 presidential election.

Mitt Romney appeared at an event in Philadelphia with Florida senator Marco Rubio, intensifying speculation about his vice-presidential running mate choice, though both sidestepped questions about a possible partnership.
After winning all five of Tuesday's primary contests, Mitt Romney launched his campaign for the presidency with a speech in New Hampshire.
Mitt Romney is to make a semi-official declaration of victory in the Republican presidential nomination race, ahead of primaries in five states.
Senior advisers to Mitt Romney criticised David Cameron's White House "love-in" with Barack Obama ahead of Romney's first visit to London for the opening of the Olympic Games.
Mitt Romney's campaign releases its first official general-election TV ad, "Day One," envisioning a Romney presidency.
Newark Mayor Cory Booker criticizes the Obama campaign's Bain Capital attack ads against Mitt Romney, calling them "nauseating."
US Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney is expected to arrive in London during the Olympics for political and trade bilaterals.
A Pew Research poll shows President Obama leading Mitt Romney 50% to 46%.
Mitt Romney is spending the weekend at a Utah ski resort retreat with Republican donors and campaign supporters after a week of campaign setbacks.
Mitt Romney's vice-presidential selection process appeared to narrow as Tim Pawlenty encouraged the campaign to look at other prospects and Marco Rubio declined to discuss the process.
Mitt Romney's campaign team moved to capitalize on announcements by some Democratic members of Congress that they intend to skip the Democratic convention.

Mitt Romney predicts a sleepless night at the White House ahead of the Supreme Court ruling on Barack Obama's healthcare reform, saying he hopes the court strikes down the legislation but will make it a campaign issue if it does not.
Mitt Romney's campaign received $4.3 million in donations from 43,000 individual donors following the Supreme Court's decision to uphold Barack Obama's healthcare reform.
Mitt Romney vowed to repeal the Affordable Care Act on his first day in office if elected president, after the Supreme Court upheld the law.
Republican governors express hope that presidential candidate Mitt Romney will win the White House election and repeal the healthcare reform law.
The Obama campaign's attacks on Mitt Romney's role at Bain Capital are described as a potentially powerful weapon against him in the presidential campaign.
Romney senior adviser Eric Fehrnstrom says Romney disagrees with the Supreme Court ruling that the individual mandate is a tax, breaking with the Republican party line.
Mitt Romney said in a CBS interview that the individual health insurance mandate is a tax, saying the Supreme Court has spoken and there is no way around it.

Mitt Romney is close to making a final decision on his vice presidential running mate, saying he has "an idea in mind," with speculation focusing on candidates including Marco Rubio, Tim Pawlenty, Kelly Ayotte, Rob Portman, Chris Christie, Bobby Jindal, Susana Martinez, and others.
Obama campaign alleges Mitt Romney may have committed a crime by misrepresenting his role at Bain Capital, while Romney's campaign denies the claim and calls for an apology.
Mitt Romney declines to comment on the controversy over US Olympic uniforms being made in China, saying he will focus on security and athletes instead.
Mitt Romney faces mounting pressure over the extent of his role at Bain Capital, as Barack Obama defends scrutiny of Romney's business record.
Mitt Romney conducts five television interviews to respond to Obama campaign attacks over his tenure at Bain Capital, including a claim he may have committed a criminal offense.
Sarah Palin says Condoleezza Rice would make a "wonderful" vice-president amid speculation that Mitt Romney is vetting Rice as a possible running mate.

Mitt Romney accused the Obama administration of "Chicago-style cronyism," claiming it gave favors to campaign contributors' businesses, while the Obama campaign dismissed the allegations as an attempt to divert attention from the Bain Capital controversy.

Mitt Romney's senior campaign adviser John Sununu apologized after suggesting President Barack Obama is un-American, a remark that the Obama campaign characterized as a "meltdown" by the Romney campaign.
Mitt Romney faces ongoing scrutiny and calls from some conservatives to release more of his tax returns amid questions about his tenure at Bain Capital.
David Cameron is to host Mitt Romney in Downing Street on Thursday during Romney's visit to London for the Olympics opening ceremony.
Mitt Romney's campaign denies that an unnamed adviser's "Anglo-Saxon heritage" comments about US-UK relations reflect Romney's views, as Romney begins an international trip with a visit to London.
Mitt Romney questions London's readiness to host the Olympic Games during his overseas trip, drawing rebukes from David Cameron and Boris Johnson.
Mitt Romney visits London on the first day of his overseas trip as the presumptive Republican nominee, where he questions London's readiness for the Olympics and offends his hosts.
US presidential candidate Mitt Romney questions London's readiness for the 2012 Olympic Games, citing "disconcerting signs" in the buildup.
US presidential hopeful Mitt Romney met with Labour leader Ed Miliband in London to exchange ideas and perspectives during a visit ahead of attending the Olympic Games opening ceremony.
Mitt Romney questions Britain's readiness for the London 2012 Olympics, prompting David Cameron to hit back and defend the Games.
Mitt Romney's Olympic comment during his visit to London stirred anger among Britons and reportedly angered David Cameron, though the reaction was largely ridicule rather than genuine fury.
Mitt Romney's campaign attempts to limit damage from his gaffe-strewn London visit, which drew mocking put-downs from London's mayor and the British prime minister and critical coverage in the US.
Mitt Romney faced a cold reception from UK media after questioning London's Olympic readiness and making diplomatic gaffes during his visit.
Former Vice President Dick Cheney said Sarah Palin was a "mistake" as the 2008 Republican vice-presidential pick and urged Mitt Romney to choose a more experienced running mate.
Obama adviser Robert Gibbs said Mitt Romney's gaffes on his London trip showed he is not ready to be US president.
Republican presidential hopeful Mitt Romney visits Israel, including holding a fundraiser at the King David Hotel in Jerusalem.
Mitt Romney's campaign launches a "Mitt's VP app" that will notify users of his running mate choice before a media announcement, though Romney has yet to announce his pick.
Mitt Romney announces congressman Paul Ryan as his vice-presidential running mate at a campaign rally in Norfolk, Virginia.
Mitt Romney chooses Paul Ryan as his vice-presidential running mate, a pick that drew enthusiastic reactions from conservatives.

Gawker published 950 pages of documents detailing aspects of Mitt Romney's investments, revealing his wealth is held through a complex network of Bain Capital-affiliated funds and Cayman Islands-based holding companies.
A Pew Research Center survey finds that media coverage of Mitt Romney's character and record during the 2012 presidential campaign was negative in 71% of stories.
Mitt Romney defended his Massachusetts healthcare record and claimed Obama would cut $700bn from Medicare.
Mitt Romney is formally nominated as the Republican presidential candidate at the party's national convention.
Mitt Romney is scheduled to use his primetime speech at the Republican National Convention to address his Mormon religion and his record as chief executive of Bain Capital.
Barack Obama criticized Mitt Romney over climate change during his re-election campaign speech, contrasting Romney's joke about climate change with his own stance that it is a real threat.

Republican presidential hopeful Mitt Romney said he would keep some of Barack Obama's healthcare reforms if elected, including coverage for people with pre-existing conditions and allowing young adults to stay on their parents' insurance.
President Barack Obama's campaign raised more than $114 million in August, surpassing Mitt Romney's $111 million, ending three straight months in which Romney had out-raised Obama.
Mitt Romney and Paul Ryan select John Kerry and Chris Van Hollen to play their rivals in mock debate sessions ahead of the October TV debates.
Mitt Romney's campaign fights to reassure donors and voters after a leaked video from a May fundraiser shows him dismissing 47% of Americans as government-dependent.
Mitt Romney's campaign recalibrates its strategy to present a clearer, more positive picture of the candidate amid signs of internal dissent and slipping poll numbers.
Mitt Romney's campaign is settling on a rescue plan to show more of him in ads, speeches, and campaign appearances, focusing on how his ideas will help regular Americans.
Mitt Romney's collapsing campaign is hurting Republican chances in key congressional races, with candidates distancing themselves from the White House ticket.
Mitt Romney trounced Barack Obama in their first debate, boosting his momentum and support in opinion polls.
Mitt Romney renounced his earlier private-fundraiser remarks that 47% of Americans were dependent on government, saying he had said something "completely wrong."
A Pew Research Center poll gives Mitt Romney a four-point lead over Barack Obama among likely voters following the first presidential debate.
Mitt Romney delivers a foreign policy speech at the Virginia Military Institute criticizing President Obama's leadership and outlining his vision for American global leadership.
Polls show Obama and Romney tied in a dead heat ahead of their second presidential debate, with Romney gaining enthusiasm and eroding Obama's leads in swing states.
Mitt Romney's campaign gains momentum in polls after Obama's first debate performance, with Romney expressing confidence about winning the presidency.
A new NBC/Wall Street Journal poll shows Barack Obama and Mitt Romney in a virtual tie at 47% each with just over two weeks until election day.

With two weeks until the 2012 US presidential election, the race between Barack Obama and Mitt Romney is described as a dead heat in national polls, though Obama still leads in key swing states such as Ohio.
Mitt Romney hosts his last big campaign event in New Hampshire, a "Final Victory Rally" at the Verizon Wireless Arena in Manchester.
Mitt Romney loses the US presidential election to Barack Obama.
Mitt Romney is announced to give his first interview since losing the presidential race, to Fox News's Chris Wallace, with the taped interview to air the following Sunday.

Mitt Romney said in his first major interview since his November 2012 election defeat that his campaign’s “real mistake” was failing to connect with minority voters and that he underestimated support for Barack Obama’s healthcare reforms.

In his first public speech since his November 2012 election defeat, Mitt Romney told the Conservative Political Action Conference that the Republican party should learn from his mistakes and listen to governors from blue and purple states such as Chris Christie.
The Republican National Committee's post-election report admits that Mitt Romney's 2012 presidential campaign was outmatched by Barack Obama's digital operation.
Mitt Romney criticizes President Obama for not telling the truth about healthcare reform, saying the Affordable Care Act's rollout undermined Obama's credibility.

Mitt Romney criticised Russian President Vladimir Putin for spending billions on the Sochi Winter Olympics as an "unsavoury" vanity project and said the International Olympic Committee should cap spending on the Games.
A Quinnipiac University poll shows Mitt Romney as the top Republican contender for the 2016 presidential nomination, leading Jeb Bush by eight points, though Romney has not declared he is running.
Mitt Romney reportedly told donors he is considering a third presidential campaign for 2016.
Mitt Romney signaled he is seriously considering another presidential run in 2016, saying he wants to help lift people out of poverty.
Mitt Romney and Jeb Bush are set to meet privately in Utah this week amid signals both are considering a 2016 presidential run.
Mitt Romney told supporters he will not run for president in 2016.
Mitt Romney announced that he would not run for the White House again, leaving his UK-based Republican donors' backing up for grabs among 2016 presidential hopefuls.
Mitt Romney was defeated by Evander Holyfield in a charity boxing bout in Salt Lake City that raised at least $1 million for CharityVision.
Mitt Romney denies rumors of a surprise presidential bid, saying "I'm not running, I'm not planning on running."

Ronna Romney McDaniel, niece of Mitt Romney, is named deputy chair of the Republican National Committee and is expected to become RNC chair in 2017, after Trump selected Rex Tillerson for secretary of state over Mitt Romney.
Mitt Romney made gaffes during his visit to London on the eve of the Olympics, casting doubt about security and questioning whether the British public was fully behind the event.
